title: Distinct distances in the kagome grid
statement: Let the kagome grid K_N be the points (a, b) of the triangular grid T_N (the points a + b w, w = e^(i pi/3), a, b >= 0, a + b <= N - 1) with a and b not both even. Removing the sublattice 2Z[w] from the triangular lattice leaves the kagome lattice (corner-sharing triangles, four unit bonds at every site); the squared distance is da^2 + da db + db^2. Determine the largest number of points of the kagome grid K_N such that all pairwise distances are different, as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 11; the headline cell is N = 13: find 9 or more such points of the region of side 13 (an upper bound is 9).
submission: Text file: one point 'a b' per line, a point of the region of side 13 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 8 points of the region of side 13 with all pairwise distances different, the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: Erdos and Guy asked for the largest subset of the n x n grid (and of the d-dimensional grid) with all pairwise distances different, a discrete relative of Golomb rulers and of Erdos's distinct distances problem; for the square grid the answer is of order n^(2/3) up to logarithmic factors (Erdos-Guy, Lefmann-Thiele). Our problems tri-distinct and tetra-distinct ask it for the triangular grid and the tetrahedral (face-centred cubic) grid. The kagome lattice (three sites per cell, corner-sharing triangles) is the lattice of the frustrated kagome antiferromagnets; it keeps three quarters of the triangular lattice. How fast the largest distinct-distance sets grow, and how they compare with the triangular grid's, is open.
references: P. Erdos, R. K. Guy, Distinct distances between lattice points, Elemente der Mathematik 25 (1970) 121-123
H. Lefmann, T. Thiele, Point sets with distinct distances, Combinatorica 15 (1995) 379-408

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: Erdos and Guy asked it for the d-dimensional grid and we for the triangular and tetrahedral grids (tri-distinct, tetra-distinct); no result was found for the kagome grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS as such (the sequences matching them, A350350, A038810, are unrelated and agree on these few terms by coincidence).
closest: P. Erdos and R. K. Guy (1970): the square and d-dimensional grids.
Our problems tri-distinct (triangular grid) and tetra-distinct (tetrahedral grid): the same question in other lattices.
novelty.benchmark: no distinct-distance family in the benchmark

baseline.text: 8 for N = 13, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/kagome-distinct.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..11: 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 13: 9 (the C(k, 2) distances are different among the 39 squared distances that occur in the region, so C(k, 2) <= 39).
